headline: Frost and dense fog early Sunday, mostly dry through Monday, then wetter, windier weather Wednesday through Friday, with Friday strongest.
summary: As of Saturday night, forecasters expect cold, damp air near the ground to bring frost and widespread dense fog early Sunday, with lows in the 30s. Fog had already begun forming in some river valleys and should spread across the lowlands overnight. A Dense Fog Advisory runs from 1 AM to 10 AM Sunday for many areas, including the city of Seattle, Everett and Marysville, the Eastside, eastern Kitsap County, Pierce and southern King County lowlands, Olympia and southern Puget Sound, Lewis and southern Thurston County lowlands, and the Chehalis River valleys. High pressure keeps western Washington mostly dry through Monday, with near-normal temperatures, morning fog and some afternoon sun breaks. Saturday's highs were expected in the low to mid 50s. On Monday, as the high pressure shifts east, there are low chances of rain, mainly along the coast and over the Olympic Peninsula. Light rain is possible into Tuesday as a weakening front crosses the region. From Wednesday on, a series of weather systems brings wetter, more unsettled weather. Friday's system looks strongest and will likely bring breezy winds, widespread lowland rain and mountain snow. Forecasters are fairly confident about the fog, frost and dry weather through Monday. Details for later in the week and next weekend are less certain, because the computer model runs show a fair amount of variability, though they are more confident that Friday's system will be the strongest.
changes: The morning's Freeze Warning, Frost Advisory and Dense Fog Advisory expired, and a new Dense Fog Advisory for early Sunday was issued that covers more of the area, including Seattle. By afternoon, forecasters added that Friday's system will likely bring breezy winds, widespread lowland rain and mountain snow, and they placed Monday's low rain chances along the coast and Olympic Peninsula.
